title: Strict quotient balancing preserves the diagram projection formula
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I$ a finitely generated ideal, $A/I$ additive torsion, and $P_n=A/I^n$ finite and perfect over $A$ for every $n\geq1$. For a scheme $T$, use its small pro-etale site, the constant ring sheaves $\underline A_T$, $\underline{P_n}_T$, and $A_T=\varprojlim_n\underline{P_n}_T$, with canonical scalar map $\underline A_T\to A_T$ and quotient projections [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. All sites are small in [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $D(A_T)$ and $D(\underline A_T)$ for unbounded derived module categories and $r_T$ for restriction along this scalar map [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op}$, $\Delta$ be its constant-diagram functor, and $Q_T=(\underline{P_n}_T)_n$ with quotient transitions. On the ringed diagram site [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], define $\mathcal R_T^aL=\Delta L\otimes^L_{\Delta A_T}Q_T$ and $\mathcal R_T^0L_0=\Delta L_0\otimes^L_{\Delta\underline A_T}Q_T$. These are actual derived strict towers. For an edge $u:U\to V$ use the canonical coefficient isomorphisms $u^{-1}A_V\cong A_U$, $u^{-1}\underline{P_n}_V\cong\underline{P_n}_U$ [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image], the ordinary ringed operations $L_u^a\dashv R_u^a$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], their strict-diagram operations $\mathscr L_u^a\dashv\mathscr R_u^a$, and the constant-coefficient counterparts $G_u\dashv R_u^0$ and $G_u\dashv R_u^{\mathcal T}$. Let $a_u:r_UL_u^a\cong G_ur_V$, $\chi_u:r_VR_u^a\cong R_u^0r_U$, $p_u:r_U\mathscr L_u^a\cong G_ur_V$ and $d_u:r_V\mathscr R_u^a\cong R_u^{\mathcal T}r_U$ be the normalized flat scalar comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction].

Let $\rho_L$ and $q_{u,L}$ be the augmentation-preserving strict quotient balancing and pullback comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-strict-quotient-scalar-balancing].

For every $f:X\to Y$ and ambient $K\in D(A_X)$ let $\pi_f^a:\mathcal R_Y^aR_f^aK\to\mathscr R_f^a\mathcal R_X^aK$ and $\pi_f^0:\mathcal R_Y^0R_f^0r_XK\to R_f^{\mathcal T}\mathcal R_X^0r_XK$ be the diagram-site projection maps, specifically the adjuncts of counit tensored with identity [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map]. Under the diagonal direct-image identifications, they satisfy
$$(R_f^{\mathcal T}\rho_K)d_{f,\mathcal R_X^aK}\,r_Y(\pi_f^a)=\pi_f^0\mathcal R_Y^0(\chi_{f,K})\rho_{R_f^aK}.$$
The comparisons and equalities hold naturally for arbitrary ambient inputs, without completeness, properness or witnesses; they are equalities in the derived category of strict diagrams, before evaluation or inverse limit.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-strict-quotient-scalar-direct-isomorphisms] for the two scalar right-mate isomorphisms. This is the independent flat scalar setup; no projection-formula compatibility is assumed by that result.

Expand quotientProjection and the two scalar direct maps as their actual Mathlib mates. The unit equation for mateEquiv and naturality of its resulting transformation show that the transpose of alpha_M followed by H(t) is G(t-sharp) followed by the right mate. Apply this to the two ordinary counits, whose transposes are identities. Thus the two projection maps are exactly the adjuncts of tau inverse followed by reduction of the counit. The scalar counit identity is mateEquiv_counit.

Invert the pullback equation supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-quotient-scalar-balancing] at the arbitrary ambient object Ra(K), cancelling p, tau, the constant reassociation and a. Naturality of rho at the completed counit, the scalar mate-counit equation, and naturality of the constant reassociation at chi identify the two adjuncts. Naturality and injectivity of the Hom equivalence for the constant diagram adjunction prove the displayed equation, in the full strict-tower derived category.

lean.statement: theorem quotientDiagramScalarProjection {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A) (bal : Balancing d) (p : PullCompatibility f d (bal.ρ Y) (bal.ρ X)) (Ra : D (ring X d true) ⥤ D (ring Y d true)) (R0 : D (ring X d false) ⥤ D (ring Y d false)) (Ha : TD (ring X d true) ⥤ TD (ring Y d true)) (H0 : TD (ring X d false) ⥤ TD (ring Y d false)) (ordinaryAdjA : p.completed.ordinary ⊣ Ra) (ordinaryAdj0 : p.constant.ordinary ⊣ R0) (diagramAdjA : p.completed.diagrams ⊣ Ha) (diagramAdj0 : p.constant.diagrams ⊣ H0) : IsIso (ordinaryScalarDirect f d bal p Ra R0 ordinaryAdjA ordinaryAdj0) ∧ IsIso (diagramScalarDirect f d bal p Ha H0 diagramAdjA diagramAdj0) ∧ ∀ K : D (ring X d true), (tdres (scalar Y d)).map ((quotientProjection f d true p.completed Ra Ha ordinaryAdjA diagramAdjA p.τ).app K) ≫ (diagramScalarDirect f d bal p Ha H0 diagramAdjA diagramAdj0).app ((reduction X d true).obj K) ≫ H0.map ((bal.ρ X).hom.app K) = (bal.ρ Y).hom.app (Ra.obj K) ≫ (reduction Y d false).map ((ordinaryScalarDirect f d bal p Ra R0 ordinaryAdjA ordinaryAdj0).app K) ≫ (quotientProjection f d false p.constant R0 H0 ordinaryAdj0 diagramAdj0 p.constantReassociation).app ((dres (scalar X d)).obj K)
lean.note: Uses the published StrictScalarBalancing.Balancing and PullCompatibility with their canonical coefficient maps and representative normalizations. Direct images are arbitrary right adjoints of these actual derived pullbacks, with adjunctions supplied; this parameterizes the unique adjunction-preserving presentation of the ordinary derived direct images. Scalar direct comparisons and projection maps are defined by the actual Mathlib mate equivalence, not unconstrained maps. Naturality is retained by defining them as natural transformations; the conclusion holds at every ambient object.
